Jukeoke itself is licensed under the **GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version** (`GPL-3.0-or-later`, see `LICENSE`). This file lists everything from other people that ends up in what we ship, with its licence, and says whether that licence lets it be distributed as part of a GPL-3.0-or-later program. It is our reading of the published licences, not legal advice. Machine-learning model weights are not shipped and are listed in [`MODELS.md`](MODELS.md).

## 1. Overall statement

**The app (player, recorder, key change, on Windows and macOS) is distributable under GPL-3.0-or-later.** Every Rust crate linked into it, both npm packages in the UI bundle, the vendored Rubber Band library (GPL-2.0-or-later) and the three fonts (SIL OFL 1.1, bundled as separate font files, which the OFL allows) are GPL-3.0-compatible; nothing in the app is proprietary. The app links no Microsoft WebView2Loader.dll (our own GPL loader replaces it) and depends only on DLLs that ship with Windows 11.

**The Windows Studio runtime is distributable, but not all of it is open source.** Its open-source parts are all GPL-3.0-compatible (permissive, LGPL, MPL-2.0, GPL-2.0-or-later). It also bundles binaries whose licences allow redistribution but are not open source: the NVIDIA CUDA libraries (about 2.7 GB: cuBLAS, cuDNN, cuFFT, NVRTC, ...; NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit EULA and cuDNN licence), the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs (Visual Studio 'Distributable Code' terms; also bundled by ctranslate2 and other wheels) and the Intel OpenMP runtime (Intel Simplified Software License). Say so plainly wherever the Studio is offered for download.

**Needs the owner's attention before a public release:**

1. **NVIDIA libraries and the GPL in one process.** The Studio process runs our GPL code (`jukeoke_studio`) and two pieces of third-party GPL code (`mutagen`, GPL-2.0-or-later, used to read lyrics embedded in tags; x264 and x265, GPL-2.0-or-later, linked into the FFmpeg that the `av` wheel bundles, although the Studio never encodes video) together with the NVIDIA libraries. Whether GPU runtime libraries count as the GPL's 'System Libraries' is not settled. Recommended: (a) as the copyright holder of Jukeoke's own code, add a GPL-3.0 section 7 additional permission, for example: *"As an additional permission under GNU GPL version 3 section 7, you may combine this program with the NVIDIA CUDA, cuBLAS, cuDNN and related runtime libraries, and the Microsoft Visual C++ and Intel OpenMP runtime libraries, and convey the result; the corresponding source need not include those libraries."*; and (b) remove the third-party GPL code from the Studio process, which no such permission covers: read embedded lyrics with PyAV (already the fallback for Matroska/WebM/AVI) instead of `mutagen`, and use an FFmpeg/PyAV build without x264/x265 (libavcodec imports them, so the two DLLs cannot simply be deleted). Neither change has been made or measured.
2. **Model weights are not covered by this file.** None are shipped in the repository or the app; the Studio downloads them when the user asks. The default `full` preset uses GPL-3.0 and Apache-2.0 weights, alignment Apache-2.0, transcription MIT, so a stick prepared with the defaults carries only redistributable weights. The `clean` preset's instrumental model (`bs_inst_resurrection_unwa`) and the 'best measured' set have **no published licence**: they may be downloaded by a user for themselves, but must not be put on a stick that is given to others, and commercial use is unclear (`MODELS.md`).
3. **Licence texts travel with the binaries.** MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0 require their notices in binary distributions. `third_party_licenses/` (generated by this script, copied to `Licenses/third-party/` on the stick and into the release archives) holds the licence and notice files of every linked Rust crate, of the UI bundle's npm packages and of the Studio packages marked 'none in wheel' in section 4; the other Python wheels keep theirs in their `*.dist-info` folders, and the fonts' `OFL.txt` files are in `Licenses/fonts/`. What could not be found is listed in `third_party_licenses/MISSING.txt` (crates whose published package has no licence file, and native code inside the `tokenizers` and `ctranslate2` wheels whose own notices those wheels do not carry).
4. **`lameenc` (LAME, LGPL-3.0-or-later)** is installed only because `demucs` declares it. Nothing imports it: `demucs.audio` (the only importer) is never loaded by the Studio (checked: importing `demucs.apply`, `demucs.states` and the Studio's modules leaves `lameenc` out of `sys.modules`), and the Studio writes only FLAC and float WAV. It is harmless (LGPL) and could be deleted from the runtime (0.2 MB).
5. **Flagged by this run** (not plainly GPL-3.0-compatible):

- CNRI-Python is part of the Python licence history (regex inherits it from CPython's sre). The FSF and CNRI disagree about the 1.6.1 choice-of-law clause; it is treated here as compatible, as CPython itself is.
- NVIDIA's CUDA libraries: redistributable under NVIDIA's EULA (Attachment A, 'Distributable' runtime files), not open source. See 'Overall statement'.
- MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: changes to those files stay MPL; it is compatible with GPL-3.0-or-later (MPL-2.0 section 3.3). Their source is on crates.io / PyPI.
- `jukeoke-studio` is our own package. Two of its files are MIT-licensed ports (section 6).
- `mutagen` (GPL-2.0-or-later) and the `av` wheel's FFmpeg with x264/x265: see section 1, item 1. `lameenc`: section 1, item 4.
- `nvidia-cublas-cu12` (cuBLAS 12 for CTranslate2) and `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12` are NVIDIA's own wheels; torch's CUDA 13 libraries are inside the `torch` wheel (section 5).

Plainly:

- **NVIDIA CUDA libraries** (cuBLAS 12 and 13, cuDNN 9, cuFFT, NVRTC, cuSPARSE, cuSOLVER, nvJitLink, CUPTI, cudart, NVTX): **redistributable, not open source**. NVIDIA's CUDA Toolkit EULA (Attachment A lists the redistributable runtime files) and the cuDNN Software License Agreement allow shipping them with an application, unmodified, with their notices. Their licence texts are in the `torch` and `nvidia-*` wheels' `*.dist-info` folders.
- **FFmpeg** (PyAV's wheel build, libavcodec 63): its own code is LGPL-3.0-or-later (`av_license()`, `--enable-version3`, no `--enable-gpl`), but the same configure line has `--enable-libx264 --enable-libx265`, and libavcodec imports the bundled x264 and x265 DLLs (**GPL-2.0-or-later**). As shipped, the combination is therefore GPL; that is compatible with Jukeoke's GPL-3.0-or-later. LAME is linked into libavcodec statically (LGPL-2.0-or-later).
- **Microsoft Visual C++ runtime** (msvcp140, vcruntime140, vcomp140, ...): copied in by the runtime build and also bundled by wheels (CTranslate2 among them); redistributable under the Visual Studio 'Distributable Code' terms, not open source. A compiler's runtime is the GPL's textbook 'System Library'.
- **Intel OpenMP runtime** (`libiomp5md`, loaded by torch and CTranslate2): Intel Simplified Software License, redistributable in binary form, not open source.
- **GCC/MinGW runtime DLLs** inside the `av` wheel: GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1 (the exception lets any program use them).

## 7. Fonts

Bundled in the UI (embedded in the app) and never loaded from the network. All three are under the **SIL Open Font License 1.1** with no Reserved Font Name, byte-identical to the upstream webfonts (not subset or modified). The OFL allows bundling fonts with any software, including GPL software, as long as the fonts are not sold on their own and the licence text accompanies them (`OFL.txt` beside each font).

## 8. Model weights

Not shipped with the app and never committed. The Studio downloads them into `Models/` when the user asks, checking a pinned SHA-256. Every model, its source, licence and whether commercial use is allowed: [`MODELS.md`](MODELS.md). Summary: default `full` preset = GPL-3.0 (anvuew vocals and karaoke) + Apache-2.0 (SYH99999 drums); `permissive` preset = MIT + Apache-2.0; `clean` preset adds an instrumental model with no published licence; alignment wav2vec2 Apache-2.0; transcription Whisper large-v3-turbo MIT.

## 9. Toolchain runtimes and system components

- **Windows app** (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`): libgcc, libstdc++ and winpthreads are linked statically (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1; winpthreads MIT-style), plus mingw-w64 start-up code (ZPL-2.1 / public domain, mingw-w64 `COPYING`). `msvcrt.dll`, the WebView2 Runtime and every other DLL the exe imports are part of Windows (checked by `app/scripts/check-windows-exe.sh`).
- **macOS app**: links only system frameworks and libSystem; WebKit is the system's.
- **Studio interpreter**: CPython 3.12 from python-build-standalone (PSF-2.0, with OpenSSL 3 Apache-2.0, SQLite public domain, libffi MIT, zlib Zlib; section 5).
